body_markdown:
Every year, in the two weeks before Kartik Shukla Shashthi, the same conversation happens in Purvanchali households across Delhi. The train ticket is waitlisted at 180. The tatkal did not confirm. Someone knows someone who can arrange a shared cab for a small fortune. And someone else quietly suggests the bus. The Delhi to Bihar bus corridor is what carries this whole conversation to a resolution, and understanding how it actually runs is what turns a stressful year into a manageable one.


## **What This Corridor Guide Covers**


This article covers the Delhi bus to Bihar Chhath season traffic pattern: how the corridor operates through Uttar Pradesh, which hub cities to target, how the last leg to Bihar towns is arranged, and the booking sequence that gets the family home in time.


Because the corridor runs largely through UP before reaching the Bihar border, the practical routes are Delhi to Gorakhpur, Delhi to Varanasi and the onward connections from there. Live schedules on the main leg sit on the[Delhi to Gorakhpur bus route page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/delhi-to-gorakhpur-bus-route) , which is one of the reliable single sources for this window.


# **Delhi Bus to Bihar in the Chhath Season: Routes, Rush and Onward Travel**


The Delhi to Bihar corridor is not one road. It is a set of corridors that fan through Uttar Pradesh into different parts of Bihar, and the right one depends on where in Bihar your family is. This guide walks through the corridor structure, the hub cities, the last leg options, and the booking approach that makes the whole thing work under Chhath pressure.


## **Why the Bus Corridor Matters More Than Usual**


Chhath is the one week of the year when train supply cannot match demand for Bihar-bound travel. Confirmed tickets on the major Delhi to Patna, Delhi to Muzaffarpur and Delhi to Darbhanga trains disappear within weeks of the reservation window opening, and the waiting lists that follow are among the longest of any Indian rail corridor.


That leaves buses to absorb the overflow. Intercity operators add capacity on the Delhi to Bihar and Delhi to eastern UP routes for this window, and the corridor becomes the practical backbone of the Chhath home travel movement. For families who missed the train booking window in September, the Delhi bus to Bihar Chhath season is not the fallback. It is the plan.


## **The Corridor: Delhi Through UP into Bihar**


The physical route from Delhi to Bihar runs through Uttar Pradesh, following the same expressway spine that connects the Yamuna Expressway to the Purvanchal Expressway and onward through eastern UP. The main hub cities on this spine, where zingbus operates confirmed routes, are Lucknow, Gorakhpur and Varanasi.


Delhi to Gorakhpur is the closest hub for anyone travelling to northern Bihar, since Gorakhpur sits near the Bihar border and gives easy onward road connections into towns like Bettiah, Motihari and Muzaffarpur. Delhi to Varanasi serves the southern Bihar and Bhojpuri belt well, with onward road access into towns like Chhapra, Ballia and beyond. Delhi to Lucknow, while further from Bihar, is a viable connector for anyone with onward road plans to central and northwest Bihar.


## **The Overnight Journey Times**


The Delhi to Gorakhpur run covers approximately 806 kilometres and takes around 14 hours 15 minutes on the current schedule, running as an overnight service that reaches Gorakhpur in the mid to late morning. Delhi to Varanasi covers roughly 794 kilometres over about 13 hours 15 minutes, with a similar overnight departure pattern. Delhi to Lucknow, at around 8 hours 20 minutes, is a shorter overnight run for anyone with onward transport arrangements from the city.


Fares on these corridors start in the mid Rs 500s to low Rs 600s for standard AC services and rise with demand through the Chhath week. In the peak week itself, expect the fares on the November 12 to 14 departures to be noticeably higher than the same route in October, which is why booking earlier matters.


## **Planning the Last Leg into Bihar**


Reaching a UP hub is only part of the journey for anyone whose home town is in the Bihar interior. The last leg is usually a state road transport bus, a shared cab from the hub city, or a family vehicle collecting from the arrival point. Each has trade offs during the festival week.


State road transport services in Bihar add extra runs for Chhath, but they fill fast and the departures are less predictable than on the intercity corridor. Shared cabs from Gorakhpur and Varanasi to Bihar towns operate at market rates that spike during Chhath, so agree the fare before boarding. If a family vehicle can meet you at the hub, that is usually the smoothest option and worth arranging well in advance rather than assumed on arrival.


## **How Demand Builds Across the Two Weeks**


The Delhi to Bihar corridor does not fill uniformly. Bookings begin picking up in early October, tighten sharply through the first week of November, and hit peak availability pressure between November 11 and 14. Return demand from the hub cities peaks late on Monday November 16, once the Usha Arghya is complete, and stays high through Tuesday.


The Chhath home travel bus corridor is one of the more predictable seasonal movements in Indian intercity travel, and the pattern repeats almost identically every year. What that means practically is that anyone booking three or four weeks ahead gets a wide choice of departure and fare, and anyone booking in the last week gets whatever remains at whatever price it is offered.


## **Comfort and Safety on the Longer Overnight Runs**


On the delhi bus to bihar chhath season corridor, the Delhi to Gorakhpur and Delhi to Varanasi runs are both 13 to 14 hour overnight journeys, which is long enough that the coach type matters. AC sleeper services with two by one berth layouts are the most common configuration on these corridors, and are noticeably easier on the body than a seater over that distance.


On the safety side, expect GPS live tracking through the app, female friendly seating options, and a two driver rotation on the longer overnight legs. For the Delhi to Lucknow and Delhi to Gorakhpur routes specifically, the Freemeal coupon applies to Plus services in normal operation, adding a meal at no extra cost. Confirm the current availability on your specific date rather than assuming a feature is offered.


## **Booking Sequence for the Chhath Week**


The sensible booking sequence for the delhi bus to bihar chhath season corridor has three steps. First, decide the arrival hub based on where in Bihar you are travelling to. Second, book the outbound Delhi departure at least three weeks ahead. Third, arrange the last leg from the hub before you leave Delhi, not after you arrive.


This last part is where most travellers slip up. The Delhi bus to Bihar Chhath season traffic is heavy enough that arriving in Gorakhpur or Varanasi at 11 AM on a Saturday with no onward plan means competing with hundreds of other passengers for the same shared cabs and buses. A confirmed onward arrangement, even a rough one with an approximate departure time, turns the corridor trip into a home trip rather than a two stage scramble.


## **Getting Home Well**


The delhi bus to bihar chhath season corridor does exactly what it needs to do: it moves large numbers of people to the right UP hub in time to make the last leg into their home town. What decides whether the journey is smooth or stressful is entirely the planning that goes in before the outbound bus leaves.


Fix the hub, book the seat early, arrange the last leg, and plan the return for after Tuesday. Handle those four decisions in September or October and the rest of the trip more or less runs itself. The corridor is built for this rush every year, and the operators know how to move volume. What no one can do for you is decide your dates late.


## **Delhi Bus to Bihar in Chhath Season: Common Questions**


The questions below cover what travellers ask most about the Chhath corridor.


### **Why is train booking so hard for Bihar during Chhath?**


Trains to Bihar fill months ahead for Chhath, with waiting lists in the hundreds. Bus corridors add capacity and become the practical route home for many Purvanchali families.


### **Which UP hubs serve the Delhi bus to Bihar Chhath season traffic?**


The main UP hubs on the Delhi bus to Bihar Chhath season corridor are Gorakhpur for northern Bihar, Varanasi for the southern Bhojpuri belt, and Lucknow as a broader connector.


### **How long is the Delhi to Gorakhpur bus journey?**


The Delhi to Gorakhpur overnight bus covers around 806 kilometres and takes approximately 14 hours 15 minutes, arriving in Gorakhpur in the mid to late morning of the next day.


### **How do I reach my Bihar town after arriving at a UP hub?**


Use a Bihar state transport bus, a shared cab, or arrange a family vehicle to meet you at the hub. Confirm the last leg before leaving Delhi rather than sorting it after arrival.


### **When should I book the Delhi bus to Bihar for Chhath 2026?**


Book by early October at the latest. Seats and fares tighten from mid October and peak between November 11 and 14, when late bookings become unreliable and expensive.


### **Which day should I depart Delhi for a Chhath 2026 trip?**


Aim for a Friday November 13 evening departure, arriving your hub Saturday morning. That leaves time to reach your Bihar home town before Kharna evening on November 14.


### **Are shared cabs from Gorakhpur to Bihar reliable during Chhath?**


Shared cabs operate but at raised festival rates. Agree the fare before boarding, and where possible, pre arrange a family vehicle pickup rather than depending on the shared market.


### **What fares should I expect in the Chhath window?**


Expect fares to start in the mid to high hundreds and rise with demand through the peak week. Early October booking usually secures the standard fare band on your date.


### **Are sleeper buses available on the Delhi to Bihar routes?**


Yes, AC sleeper services with two by one berth layouts are common on the Delhi to Gorakhpur and Delhi to Varanasi corridors, which suits the 13 to 14 hour overnight run.


### **Is there a meal service on these overnight routes?**


Delhi to Gorakhpur and Delhi to Lucknow are two of the three named routes where the Freemeal coupon applies to Plus services in normal operation. Confirm on your date.


### **When should I plan the return from the hub to Delhi?**


Plan the return for Tuesday November 17 or later, since Monday night is the peak return rush after the Usha Arghya, and Tuesday travel usually means better fares and seats.


### **What documents do I need for the corridor trip?**


Carry a valid government photo ID for the booking and the journey. Keep a printed or app copy of the ticket, and share the schedule with someone at home for safety.
